en.bay.lead.after: that read handwritten Baybayin from a webcam in real time, using OpenCV optical flow and a GRU recurrent network. This is the easy half of that problem, running entirely in your browser.
en.bay.note: Baybayin is an abugida: every consonant already carries an a. A mark above switches it to i or e, a mark below to u or o, and a virama cancels the vowel entirely. It is a lookup table and a state machine — no model, no network call, and the same input always gives the same output. Knowing when not to reach for an LLM is part of the job.
en.bay.draw.heading: Now the other way round
en.bay.draw.lead: Draw a Baybayin character and it will guess which one. This is the inverse problem the Baybayin Detector solved from a webcam.
en.bay.draw.empty: Draw a character above to see a guess.
en.bay.draw.method: Template matching against glyphs rendered from the page font. No model, no download, about a millisecond.

fil.bay.lead.before: Noong 2024 ay katuwang akong gumawa ng
fil.bay.lead.after: na bumabasa ng sulat-kamay na Baybayin mula sa webcam nang real time, gamit ang OpenCV optical flow at GRU recurrent network. Ito ang mas madaling kalahati ng problemang iyon, tumatakbo lahat sa browser mo.
fil.bay.note: Ang Baybayin ay abugida: bawat katinig ay may kasamang a. Ang guhit sa itaas ay ginagawa itong i o e, ang guhit sa ibaba ay u o o, at ang virama ay tinatanggal ang patinig. Isa itong lookup table at state machine — walang modelo, walang network call, at pareho ang labas sa parehong input. Bahagi ng trabaho ang malaman kung kailan hindi dapat gumamit ng LLM.
